text: Softer section colours, and the home Guides are cards again.
"Need help now?" sits in the header, phone menus open one group at a time, and pages load faster.
New "On this page" box, and shortages the TGA expects soon now show with their start date.
Shows when a shortage is expected to start.
Supply now tracks more brands: hormones, doxycycline, Epiduo, Regaine, Mirena, vaginal oestrogen and menopause tablets.
Home page: the Guides section now lists the five menus, with every page in each.
Menus reorganised into Your medicines, Supply, Family & carers, Clinicians and About.
New Easy Read guide for parents and carers of under-18s.
Page sections now have named links, so you can share a link to one part of a page.
Clearer openings for the GnRH medicines page and the ally guide.
Grouped citations now link to the numbered references; reference fixes across the site.
Dark mode: the Supply colour is now Old gold.
New page: first steps, care at the Women’s and Children’s Hospital, consent and support for parents of under-18s.
Potassium and kidney tests: before you start and at regular reviews, sooner if you have kidney problems.
New page: a GP guide to starting adult hormone therapy, from the 2026 AusPATH standards.
Renamed Your medicines: start here.
Renamed Stock seen by patients.
Renamed Doses and formulations.
Renamed Fertility, PrEP and surgery.
Renamed Helping an adult with their medicines.
Renamed Clinician reference.
New Toolkit group in the menu: authority card, injection training, monitoring schedule.
Renamed Other services and links.
Renamed Guides to print.
Shortage cards and the checked date now show as soon as the page opens.
Patches: the same labelled strength of Estradot and Estraderm MX gives the same daily dose; size and adhesive differ.
Record logs: the QR code on each log now opens the page that explains it.
Menus: the section for health professionals is now called Clinicians.
Inclusive environment checklist: new note to check your software can record both a chosen name and a Medicare name.
Pages now load with less jumping around, so they settle faster on phones and slow connections.
Every medicine page has a clearer search title, description and more common questions answered.
Download bubbles now always end their paragraph, after the full stop.
Shorter header search box, and the Accessibility button now says so in words on wider screens (icon only on phones).
High-contrast mode fixed: the header menu and every page now pass colour-contrast checks.
The home page drawing now plays once and stops instead of repeating.
We now count downloads of each file and outreach link tags as daily totals only, with nothing about you; see Privacy.
New page: every GAMSA guide, checklist, log and form in one place, grouped by who it is for.
Printables cut to the pharmacy ones; a link now leads to all our guides and printables.
Dose and symptom logs to print now sit at the end of this page.
PBS source notes are shorter, still showing the source, the extraction date and that the text is not GAMSA’s own.
Each medicine now has its own short “Reading your results” points, also in its printable blood test guide.
Blood test sheets are now called blood test guides; old links still work.
Inclusive environment checklist added to the clinician downloads.
Reference to the injection procedure updated to version 2.6 (7 November 2026).
Fewer text sizes, with page intros the size of body text. Tidier download cards; full stops sit before download buttons.
PBS restriction wording now quoted word for word, with its PBS source and extraction date beside it.
PBS criteria for the Authority quoted word for word, with their source and date.
Added the PBS source and extraction date for the Femoston listing.
PBS acknowledgement: reproduced with permission; the PBS Schedule in force on the day governs.
Says where the PBS amounts come from and when we checked them.
Authority wording card updated to version 1.7: PBS prescribing instruction quoted word for word, GAMSA's explanation labelled.
PBS figures on every page now show their source, www.pbs.gov.au, and the date they were extracted.
Now called Blood tests and monitoring: one section for each medicine and form, each with a blood test guide to print.
New page: fertility, sexual function, PrEP and hormones around surgery, moved from the Monitoring page.
What is monitored now matches the Blood tests page, with a Blood tests box and a blood test guide to print.
New short paragraph on monitoring and lab units, linking the Blood tests and monitoring page.
The monitoring schedule is now one blood test guide for each medicine and form.
Links to fertility, sexual function, PrEP and surgery now go to the new Related care page.
Less space between each page's summary, buttons and Updated note.
Blood tests: when to have them, reading lab results, the Blood tests and monitoring page and logs you can print.
Who gives the long-acting injection, the page to take home after it, and that it is not self-injected.
Shortage cards now list each brand that is hard to get and when it should be back.
Supply notices are now grouped by medicine and strength.
New: brand premiums, and how to ask for a brand with no premium.
In some places, a trained pharmacist can give the long-acting injection.
Now points to the Blood tests and monitoring page for the usual tests for each medicine.
The guides are now checked whenever the website changes, and each shows the date it was last checked.
Training package 2.6: respectful-appointment steps, yearly reassessment, a quiz and a patient after-injection handout.
Card labels now show real dates and page counts.
Zoladex consumer information is no longer on the Medicine Finder; the reference now points to the TGA search.
Downloads no longer carry an amendment history table; the version and date stay on each page.
Printables can now be filled in on screen, then printed; each file is locked so the layout cannot be changed.
Blood test guides: tick boxes you can fill in on screen, and every guide now fits on one or two pages.
Pharmacy visit checklist: tick boxes you can fill in on screen, then print.
Downloads end with the GAMSA copyright line and are locked (fill in and print, not edit). Training package now all v2.6.
Training package: all five documents now version 2.6; the PDFs are locked, so forms can be filled in and printed, not edited.
New printables: dose and symptom logs, a monitoring schedule and an inclusive-environment checklist.
New tables of the tests to expect for each medicine: before starting, in the first year, then yearly.
Training documents v2.5 add hand hygiene, patient identity and needlestick steps. PBS card v1.6.
Zoladex 3.6 mg is still on the PBS after 1 November 2026. The 1 May 2027 end date comes from AstraZeneca, not the PBS.
PBS figures now name the PBS as their source, with the date they were taken from it.
Brand premium wording is now neutral: "If you would rather not pay one, ask your pharmacist for a brand with no premium."
Reports, sightings and feedback are now kept for 12 months, then deleted.
Supply and shortage lists now show the newest changes first.
Rewritten: why GAMSA was made and who runs it, with an Ahpra registration number.
Page titles now say South Australia in full, and the site footer says "All rights reserved".

The Medicines, doses and formulations page is now two pages. Medicines, doses and formulations keeps the forms and dose ranges of each medicine. A new Monitoring and related care page has blood tests and reviews, getting the timing of a blood test right, fertility, sexual function, PrEP, and hormones around surgery. The words have not changed; reference numbers on both pages have been renumbered. On the home page, a new drawing of a dispensing set has a pump that pours the guide ribbon, the heading above the four cards now reads "Guides", and the Trans card links to Monitoring and to Add-on therapies.
Hormones around surgery and the Resources page now link to TransHub's pages on each gender-affirming surgery and to the Trans Health SA practitioner directory.

Bicalutamide safety points added from the Australian product information: it can make warfarin work more strongly (closer INR blood tests), it can rarely make skin burn more easily in the sun, and, for clinicians, its CYP3A4 interactions. The TGA safety update for the lung warning (interstitial lung disease) is now listed as a second source.

PBS prices and the co-payment are now dated. Five page titles (Angeliq, Estalis, Femoston, Kliogest and Trisequens) now start with the generic name. Two brand comparisons were reworded to be neutral, and an unsourced claim about steadier levels was removed.
New page: Add-on therapies. Treatments for acne, scalp hair loss, periods that continue on testosterone and vaginal dryness now have their own page, moved from the doses guide.
New section on the doses guide: Hormones around surgery. It explains the clot risk with major surgery and why talking with your surgeon and prescriber early matters.
PrEP wording is clearer: Australian guidelines suggest anyone on hormones (including those with a vagina) should take PrEP every day, not only around the time of sex.
The sexual function section on oestrogen and blockers is reworded in plainer clinical language. The facts are the same.

The doses guide now explains testosterone PBS rules: why an Authority is needed, which injections are listed, the patches that were cancelled, and e-scripts. The testosterone medicine pages link to it.
The privacy page is rewritten to be shorter and more formal. It still covers everything we collect, who can see it and how to have it removed.
The contact email, gamsaenquiries@gmail.com, now appears on more pages. The feedback form is still the preferred way to reach us.
The five injection training documents are now version 2.4 and the PBS Authority wording card is version 1.5. The injection-site drawing matches the one on this site.
Every medicine page now has a dated “Available in Australia?” line, linked to the supply page.
The supply page now tracks triptorelin (Diphereline), isotretinoin and finasteride, and names each isotretinoin brand that is out of stock with its expected return date.
Zoladex is PBS-listed until 1 May 2027.
Pharmacists now post stock reports with a personal report key, sent after their first approved report. Published reports show stock facts only.
Patient sightings are now marked “Unverified”.
The injection SOP and training guide is now version 2.3: Figure 1 steps 5 and 6 match this site.
Each medicine page now has a Print or save as PDF button and a Read aloud button.
Added a safety note on bicalutamide: not a first choice, regular liver tests, and the new lung warning in its product information.
Added PrEP and hormones: no interaction, take PrEP every day, and keep up kidney tests, especially with spironolactone.
Added the 2026 standards of care view on oestradiol implants next to the earlier caution.
Added the 2026 standards of care view on hormones and clot risk around surgery.
New section on fertility before starting hormones: storing sperm or eggs is optional, may delay starting, and costs differ.
New section on sexual function on oestrogen and blockers, with the options in the 2026 standards of care.
New Getting care section: Medicare items, prescriber directories, surgery links, neurodivergence, and questions about testosterone scripts.
New About page: who runs the site, how pages are made and reviewed, corrections, complaints and an accessibility statement.
Reworded opening lines to remove ranking words and to give the main risk next to the benefits.
Corrected the backup line: the monthly backup is being set up and has not started yet.
Easy Read guides: long lines made shorter, one sentence per line, and pictures that match the words.
Injection training package: all five documents are now version 2.3, each with a document ID, an amendment table and a next review date (24 October 2027).
Treatment-room card: the landmark key now sits under its heading, and the card says to check the QR code for the current version.
PBS Authority wording card, version 1.4: new print fonts, a document ID and a next review date. The wording is the same.
Safety notes on medicine pages now show, such as when to call 000 and which medicines to tell your pharmacist about.
Safety wording on five medicine pages now matches the product information.
The PBS cost section is brought up to date with the current PBS listing.
A brand that carries its own premium is no longer listed as “No premium” (Spiractin, Doryx). Where every brand of a medicine carries a premium, the page says so.
The testosterone injection documents are now version 2.2, with one A4 layout and larger tick boxes. The PBS Authority wording card and the pharmacy visit checklist are version 1.3.
Observation after the long-acting testosterone injection is now at least 30 minutes.
Doses and blood test targets now follow the AusPATH 2026 standards of care. Where guidelines differ, the page says which one it follows.
New safety point from the medicine leaflets: testosterone taken with an SGLT-2 inhibitor (a diabetes, heart or kidney medicine) can raise the red blood cell count.
New safety point from the medicine leaflet: meningioma.
New safety points from the medicine leaflets: rare severe skin reactions, heart rhythm (QT) checks and mood changes.
Triptorelin is now on the PBS, but not for gender dysphoria under 18, so puberty blockers stay private scripts for young people.
The supply page now shows when limited medicines are expected back.
The patch diagram now places every spot where the leaflets say: the lower belly or the buttocks.
Depo-Ralovera is marked as no longer available in Australia. Depo-Provera is the injection.
TGA shortage alerts are now available as an RSS feed at gamsa.au/feed.xml.
“Need help now?” now lists SA Mental Health Triage (13 14 65) and 13YARN (13 92 76), with tap-to-call numbers.
